project.name: invoice-wallet
project.description: Local-first Taiwan e-invoice wallet — Android Kotlin monorepo (Compose + Hilt + Room/SQLCipher + CameraX + ML Kit + zxing-cpp) plus a Go relay-server (gorilla/websocket) for self-hosted AI access via the Model Context Protocol.

nodes.name: HomeScreenSmokeTest.kt
nodes.summary: Instrumented (AndroidJUnit4) smoke test that renders InvoiceListScreen with an empty UiState inside InvoiceWalletTheme and asserts the '還沒有發票' empty-state copy is shown.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ComposeRule + AndroidJUnit4 — runs on a real device/emulator without launching the full Activity or Hilt graph.

nodes.name: HomeScreenSmokeTest
nodes.summary: Test class with a single @Test that verifies the home (invoice list) screen renders the empty-state when the wallet has no invoices.

nodes.name: InvoiceWalletApp.kt
nodes.summary: Root navigation Composable: hosts a Scaffold with WalletNavBar bottom-bar plus a NavHost wiring the three top-level tabs (發票/對獎/設定) and the scan, detail, and pairing sub-routes. nodes.name: InvoiceWalletApp
nodes.summary: Top-level app Composable. Builds the NavController, decides when to show the bottom bar (only on LIST/LOTTERY/SETTINGS routes), and wires every navigation destination of the wallet.

nodes.name: ScanRoute

nodes.name: MainActivity

nodes.name: MainActivityTest
nodes.summary: Robolectric-driven Compose smoke test class that renders InvoiceListScreen empty state and asserts the localized empty-state string.

nodes.name: CategoryGuesser
nodes.summary: Singleton object holding the 8-category slug list, label lookup, drawable lookup, and the ordered regex rule table for merchant classification.

nodes.name: SectionLabel.kt

nodes.name: WalletNavBar.kt

nodes.name: WalletNavItem

nodes.name: WalletTheme
nodes.summary: Top-level theme Composable: installs wallet token providers and delegates to MaterialTheme for cross-compatibility with stray M3 widgets.

nodes.name: InvoiceListScreen.kt

nodes.name: InvoiceListRoute
nodes.summary: Route-entry Composable wiring InvoiceListViewModel + nav callbacks (scan, invoice click, lottery, settings) into the stateless InvoiceListScreen.

nodes.name: InvoiceListScreen
nodes.summary: Stateless Compose home screen — query field, category pill filter row, empty state, and the invoice list with relative-date grouping headers.

nodes.name: LotteryScreen.kt
nodes.summary: 對獎 (lottery-check) tab Composable — shows the current period's winning numbers grouped by prize tier with a refresh action, plus a back navigation button.

nodes.name: LotteryRoute

nodes.name: LotteryScreen
nodes.summary: Renders the period header, refresh CompactPill, prize-tier sections of LotteryNumber rows, and empty-state copy.

nodes.name: CameraQrScanner.kt
nodes.summary: CameraX-backed live QR scanner Composable that binds Preview + ImageAnalysis, runs ML Kit barcode scanning, and emits paired left/right Taiwan e-invoice QR payloads to the caller.

nodes.name: CameraQrScanner
nodes.summary: Binds CameraX use cases, runs ML Kit QR detection in an ImageAnalysis analyzer, and invokes onInvoiceQr with the left/right code halves once both have been seen.

nodes.name: ScanScreen.kt
nodes.summary: Stateless Compose screen for the scan flow. Switches between Idle / Loading / NeedsConfirmation / Success / Duplicate / Failed ScanState branches, hosts the cameraContent slot, and exposes pick-image / confirm / cancel callbacks.

nodes.name: ScanScreen
nodes.summary: Renders the scan flow UI: an embedded cameraContent slot, scan-state-driven Cards, and the bottom action row (cancel + pick image / confirm).

nodes.name: SettingsScreen.kt
nodes.summary: 設定 (settings) tab Composable. Exposes theme-mode, default-scan-mode, export-format choices via PillChip rows, and CTAs for relay pairing and onboarding replay, all driven by SettingsViewModel state.

nodes.name: SettingsRoute
nodes.summary: Route-entry Composable hosting SettingsViewModel and forwarding state plus chooser callbacks (theme, scan mode, export, pair relay, onboarding) into SettingsScreen.

nodes.name: SettingsScreen
nodes.summary: Stateless settings UI grouped by SectionLabel rows: theme, scan-mode, export format, relay pairing, replay onboarding, plus app meta info.

nodes.name: OnboardingScreen.kt
nodes.summary: First-run onboarding pager — sequence of OnboardingPage entries with illustration, title, body, and a PillButton CTA that advances or finishes (invoking onFinish on the last page).

nodes.name: OnboardingScreen
nodes.summary: Hosts the HorizontalPager-driven onboarding flow with page indicator and CTA that advances or calls onFinish.

nodes.name: OnboardingPage
nodes.summary: Immutable data class describing a single onboarding page: title, body, and DrawableRes illustration.

nodes.name: OnboardingScreenTest.kt
nodes.summary: Robolectric Compose test for OnboardingScreen verifying the pager advances through pages and that the final CTA invokes onFinish.

nodes.name: OnboardingScreenTest
nodes.summary: Test class asserting onboarding pager flow and the onFinish callback contract.

nodes.name: InvoiceWalletDatabaseTest.kt
nodes.summary: AndroidJUnit4 instrumentation test that builds an in-memory Room database and verifies the Invoice entity round-trips through TypeConverters and the asEntity/asExternalModel mappers.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Room.inMemoryDatabaseBuilder so the SQLCipher native lib isn't required for this smoke test; runs under AndroidJUnit4 because Room code-gen needs an Android runtime.

nodes.name: TestEntities.kt
nodes.summary: Internal builder helpers (invoiceEntity, invoiceItemEntity, lotteryNumberEntity, authGrantEntity, queryAuditLogEntity) that produce fully-defaulted Room entities for use across the androidTest suite.

nodes.name: AuthGrantDaoTest.kt
nodes.summary: Instrumentation test covering AuthGrantDao upsert/getById, observeActive (excludes revoked), and revoke timestamp stamping against an in-memory Room database.

nodes.name: InvoiceDaoTest.kt
nodes.summary: Instrumentation test for InvoiceDao covering insert/duplicate-abort, date-range observation, soft-delete semantics, merchant lookup, and Turbine-asserted Flow emissions.

nodes.name: InvoiceItemDaoTest.kt
nodes.summary: Instrumentation test for InvoiceItemDao verifying batch insert ordered by sequence, deleteByInvoiceId cascade, and observeByInvoiceId Flow emissions.

nodes.name: LotteryNumberDaoTest.kt
nodes.summary: Instrumentation test for LotteryNumberDao covering upsert idempotency on the period primary key and getLatest selecting the highest period.

nodes.name: QueryAuditLogDaoTest.kt
nodes.summary: Instrumentation test for QueryAuditLogDao verifying append-only insert ordering and countSince threshold behaviour used by the rate-limiter.

nodes.name: DatabasePassphraseProvider.kt
nodes.summary: Generates and persists a 32-byte SQLCipher passphrase inside EncryptedSharedPreferences, whose AES256_GCM master key is held in the Android Keystore so the raw key never sits in plaintext on disk.
nodes.languageNotes: EncryptedSharedPreferences + MasterKey is the AndroidX-canonical way to hardware-bind a derived secret; the lazy delegate ensures the master key is only created once per process.

nodes.name: InvoiceWalletDatabase.kt
nodes.summary: Room database root: declares the five entities (invoices, invoice_items, lottery_numbers, auth_grants, query_audit_log) at schema v1, the Converters typed-converter bundle, and abstract DAO accessors.
nodes.languageNotes: exportSchema = true causes KSP to emit the JSON schema file used for migration tests; abstract class + Room.databaseBuilder produces the generated implementation at build time.

nodes.name: AuthGrantDao.kt
nodes.summary: Room DAO for the auth_grants table — upsert/get/revoke a grant plus a Flow of non-revoked grants for the consent UI.

nodes.name: InvoiceDao.kt
nodes.summary: Room DAO for the invoices table: strict insert (ABORT on duplicate invoice_number), upsert, lookups by id/invoice-number/merchant, date-range and full-text-ish search Flows, and soft delete.

nodes.name: InvoiceItemDao.kt
nodes.summary: Room DAO for invoice_items: bulk insert with REPLACE conflict strategy, list/observe by invoice id (ordered by sequence), and cascade-delete by invoice id.

nodes.name: LotteryNumberDao.kt
nodes.summary: Room DAO for lottery_numbers keyed by period: upsert, getByPeriod, observeAll, and getLatest used by the lottery-redemption checker.

nodes.name: QueryAuditLogDao.kt
nodes.summary: Append-only Room DAO for query_audit_log: insert one log row, list by grant, and countSince timestamp — the latter feeds the per-grant rate limiter slated for Iteration 6.

nodes.name: DatabaseModule.kt
nodes.summary: Hilt SingletonComponent module wiring the SQLCipher-encrypted database, all five DAOs, the system clock, and the Room-backed Invoice/Lottery/AuthGrant repositories into the app's DI graph.

nodes.name: AuthGrantEntity.kt
nodes.summary: Room entity for the auth_grants table — stores a third-party client's permission scope, optional excluded categories, granted/expires/revoked timestamps.

nodes.name: InvoiceEntity.kt
nodes.summary: Room entity for invoices (ARCHITECTURE section 5.1) with unique index on invoice_number and supporting indices on issue_date and merchant_tax_id; enums (source, lotteryStatus) stored as their name string.
nodes.languageNotes: carrierIdEncrypted holds a pre-encrypted payload from the carrier-CSV path; the column itself is opaque to Room — encryption lives outside this layer.

nodes.name: InvoiceItemEntity.kt
nodes.summary: Room entity for invoice_items with a non-unique index on invoice_id; carries the line-item name, quantity, unit price, amount, optional category, and a sequence number for display order.

nodes.name: LotteryNumberEntity.kt
nodes.summary: Room entity for lottery_numbers keyed by period (e.g. 11502), holding special/grand prize numbers, the first-prize list, additional sixth-digit numbers, and the fetched-at timestamp.

nodes.name: QueryAuditLogEntity.kt
nodes.summary: Room entity for query_audit_log: one row per tool invocation by a grant, indexed on grant_id for the rate-limit COUNT query.

nodes.name: Mappers.kt
nodes.summary: Pair of asEntity/asExternalModel extension functions for each of the five Room entities, translating between the persistence shape (enums as strings) and the core domain model (typed enums).
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin extension functions keep the persistence-to-domain boundary one-way and reflection-free; uses Enum.valueOf for string round-trip, which will throw at read time if a stored enum string drifts from the model.

nodes.name: RoomLotteryRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Implements LotteryRepository by delegating to LotteryNumberDao and translating entities to LotteryNumber domain models via the mapper extensions.

nodes.name: Fakes.kt
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled in-memory fake implementations of all five DAOs (FakeInvoiceDao, FakeInvoiceItemDao, FakeLotteryNumberDao, FakeAuthGrantDao, FakeQueryAuditLogDao) so repository logic can be exercised in pure JVM unit tests off-device.
nodes.languageNotes: Each fake backs state with a MutableStateFlow so observe* methods can re-emit through map operators, mirroring Room's invalidation semantics without needing the Android runtime.

nodes.name: InvoiceWalletDatabase
nodes.summary: Abstract RoomDatabase at schema version 1 declaring all five entities and the Converters TypeConverters; exposes one abstract DAO accessor per table.

nodes.name: DatabasePassphraseProvider
nodes.summary: Generates a 32-byte SecureRandom passphrase on first call and persists it in EncryptedSharedPreferences (master key in the Android Keystore); subsequent calls return the existing key.

nodes.name: AuthGrantDao
nodes.summary: Room DAO interface for auth_grants: upsert, getById, observeActive (revoked_at IS NULL), and revoke (stamps revoked_at).

nodes.name: InvoiceDao
nodes.summary: Room DAO interface for the invoices table with nine methods covering strict insert, upsert, id/invoice-number/merchant lookups, date-range observation, LIKE search with limit, and soft delete.

nodes.name: InvoiceItemDao
nodes.summary: Room DAO interface for invoice_items: insertAll (REPLACE on conflict), getByInvoiceId, observeByInvoiceId (Flow), and deleteByInvoiceId.

nodes.name: LotteryNumberDao
nodes.summary: Room DAO interface for lottery_numbers keyed by period: upsert, getByPeriod, observeAll, getLatest.

nodes.name: QueryAuditLogDao
nodes.summary: Append-only Room DAO interface for query_audit_log: insert, getByGrant ordered newest-first, and countSince for the per-grant rate limiter.

nodes.name: DatabaseModule
nodes.summary: Hilt @Module installed in SingletonComponent providing the passphrase provider, the SQLCipher-encrypted Room database, every DAO, a system Clock, and the three Room-backed repository singletons.

nodes.name: AuthGrantEntity
nodes.summary: Room @Entity (tableName = auth_grants) data class with the grant id PK, client_name, channel, scopes/excluded_categories lists, optional date_range_days, and granted/expires/revoked timestamps.

nodes.name: InvoiceEntity
nodes.summary: Room @Entity (tableName = invoices) data class with 24 columns, unique index on invoice_number and supporting indices on issue_date and merchant_tax_id; carries denormalised merchant + lottery + soft-delete fields.

nodes.name: InvoiceItemEntity
nodes.summary: Room @Entity (tableName = invoice_items) data class with non-unique index on invoice_id; one row per line item with quantity, unit price, amount, and display sequence.

nodes.name: LotteryNumberEntity
nodes.summary: Room @Entity (tableName = lottery_numbers) data class keyed by period string, holding the special/grand prize numbers, first-prize list, additional sixth-digit list, and fetched-at timestamp.

nodes.name: QueryAuditLogEntity
nodes.summary: Room @Entity (tableName = query_audit_log) data class with a non-unique index on grant_id; carries the tool name, result count and executed-at timestamp for each tool invocation.

nodes.name: RoomLotteryRepository
nodes.summary: Implements LotteryRepository by delegating each call to LotteryNumberDao and translating entities via the mapper extensions; the observeAll Flow maps row lists element-wise.

nodes.name: FakeInvoiceDao
nodes.summary: In-memory InvoiceDao fake backed by a MutableStateFlow that simulates the UNIQUE invoice_number constraint, soft-delete filtering, date-range observation, and the keyword search/limit semantics.

nodes.name: FakeInvoiceItemDao
nodes.summary: In-memory InvoiceItemDao fake using a MutableStateFlow; getByInvoiceId/observeByInvoiceId sort by sequence to match Room behaviour.

nodes.name: FakeLotteryNumberDao
nodes.summary: In-memory LotteryNumberDao fake keyed by period; upsert dedupes on period and getLatest returns the maximum period.

nodes.name: FakeAuthGrantDao
nodes.summary: In-memory AuthGrantDao fake; observeActive filters revoked_at != null and revoke stamps the timestamp on a copy of the matching row.

nodes.name: FakeQueryAuditLogDao
nodes.summary: Append-only in-memory QueryAuditLogDao fake using a plain MutableList; countSince and getByGrant filter on grantId and executedAt.

nodes.name: AppViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: App-root Hilt ViewModel that exposes persisted AppSettings as a StateFlow and reacts to MCP/relay toggle changes by starting or stopping the local MCP server and relay client.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses kotlinx.coroutines Flow.map + distinctUntilChanged inside viewModelScope to bind settings to side-effect lifecycle.

nodes.name: AppViewModel
nodes.summary: HiltViewModel that materializes settings as a StateFlow and orchestrates MCP server + RelayManager lifecycle from settings toggles. Also exposes completeOnboarding.

nodes.name: RoomRepositoryIntegrationTest.kt
nodes.summary: AndroidJUnit4 instrumentation test that exercises RoomInvoiceRepository, RoomLotteryRepository, and RoomAuthGrantRepository against a real in-memory Room database (white-box integration tier).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Room.inMemoryDatabaseBuilder with ApplicationProvider; round-trips via Flow.first() and runTest.

nodes.name: RoomRepositoryIntegrationTest
nodes.summary: Integration suite verifying that each room repository (invoice, lottery, auth-grant) round-trips correctly through the real Room SQLite engine.

nodes.name: AuthGrantRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Repository interface boundary defining AI-client authorization-grant access plus its associated query audit log (ARCHITECTURE §5.1).

nodes.name: AuthGrantRepository
nodes.summary: Repository contract for auth-grant CRUD, active-grant observation, revocation, audit-log writes, and rate-limit window counting.

nodes.name: RoomAuthGrantRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Room-backed implementation of AuthGrantRepository that maps DAO rows to domain models and stamps revocation timestamps from an injected Clock.

nodes.name: RoomAuthGrantRepository
nodes.summary: Bridges AuthGrantDao + QueryAuditLogDao to the AuthGrantRepository contract, converting via asEntity/asExternalModel mappers and using an injectable Clock for testable revocation timestamps.

nodes.name: RoomAuthGrantRepositoryTest.kt
nodes.summary: JVM unit tests for RoomAuthGrantRepository using hand-rolled fake DAOs and a fixed Clock, asserting revoke timestamp stamping and audit-count windowing.

nodes.name: AuthGrant.kt
nodes.summary: Serializable AuthGrant data class — the record of access granted to an external AI client (channel, scopes, exclusions, lifetime).

nodes.name: QueryAuditLog.kt
nodes.summary: Serializable QueryAuditLog data class — one audited tool invocation against the wallet, used for rate-limit accounting and transparency.

nodes.name: AuthorizationEngine.kt
nodes.summary: Turns an AuthGrant into an allow/deny decision for a single MCP tool call (revoked/expired/out-of-scope/rate-limit checks) and audits every served call (ARCHITECTURE §6/§11).

nodes.name: AuthorizationEngine
nodes.summary: Core authorization policy class — produces AuthDecision (Allowed with QueryConstraints, or Denied with DenyReason) and records audit entries via AuthGrantRepository.

nodes.name: AuthDecision
nodes.summary: Sealed interface result type for an authorization check — Allowed(grantId, constraints) or Denied(reason).

nodes.name: AuthorizationEngineTest.kt
nodes.summary: Kotest+JUnit5 suite covering every AuthorizationEngine path: unknown/revoked/expired/out-of-scope/rate-limit deny cases plus wildcard, date-window, and audit-recording allow cases.

nodes.name: McpDispatcher.kt
nodes.summary: Stateless MCP/JSON-RPC 2.0 dispatcher over raw request/response strings — supports initialize, tools/list, tools/call (with authorize+audit), and ignores notifications. The Ktor route is a thin adapter on top.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure string-in/string-out so it can be unit-tested without an HTTP engine — same dispatcher feeds both the local server and the relay path.

nodes.name: McpDispatcher
nodes.summary: Routes parsed JSON-RPC messages to initialize/tools-list/tools-call handlers, builds canonical success/error envelopes, and pipes every tool call through the injected authorize + onResult lambdas.

nodes.name: McpServerManager.kt
nodes.summary: Single app-facing entry point for the local MCP server — owns the controller, exposes the Bearer token, seeds the LOCAL_MCP AuthGrant on first start, and wires the AuthorizationEngine into every served call.

nodes.name: McpServerManager
nodes.summary: @Singleton Hilt-injected manager implementing McpServerControls: start/stop the local MCP server (loopback or LAN), regenerate Bearer token, and idempotently seed the local-mcp grant.

nodes.name: McpTokenStore.kt
nodes.summary: Token storage interface plus a Keystore-backed EncryptedSharedPreferences implementation that mints 32 random bytes as URL-safe Base64 and never writes the Bearer token to plaintext disk.

nodes.name: EncryptedMcpTokenStore
nodes.summary: Concrete McpTokenStore using AES256-GCM EncryptedSharedPreferences (master key in Android Keystore); generates 32-byte SecureRandom tokens encoded URL-safe Base64.

nodes.name: McpServerModule.kt
nodes.summary: Hilt SingletonComponent module wiring the AuthorizationEngine, EncryptedMcpTokenStore, and McpServerControls (binding McpServerManager).

nodes.name: RelayManager.kt
nodes.summary: Drives the RELAY path — keeps an outbound WebSocket to the relay open while enabled, answering forwarded MCP calls with the same dispatcher/tools as the local server, under a RELAY grant. Auto-reconnects with backoff.
nodes.languageNotes: Coroutine SupervisorJob + isActive reconnect loop; Ktor OkHttp engine with WebSockets plugin.

nodes.name: RelayManager
nodes.summary: @Singleton Hilt-injected lifecycle owner for the relay WebSocket — only starts if the device is paired, seeds the RELAY AuthGrant idempotently, and rebuilds the dispatcher on each start.

nodes.name: RelayMessageHandler.kt
nodes.summary: Translates a relay WebSocket envelope (mcp_request) into an mcp_response by delegating to the same McpDispatcher the local server uses, so remote and local answers stay identical.

nodes.name: RelayMessageHandler
nodes.summary: Stateless envelope translator — parses mcp_request frames, runs payload through McpDispatcher, wraps result as mcp_response. Returns null for unknown/non-request frames.

nodes.name: RelayMessageHandlerTest.kt
nodes.summary: Kotest+JUnit5 unit tests verifying mcp_request envelopes are wrapped into mcp_response and unrelated frames are ignored, using a stub McpTool through a real McpDispatcher.

nodes.name: AppSettings.kt
nodes.summary: User-controlled, non-sensitive app preferences data class (theme, default scan mode, onboarding/MCP/remote toggles) plus the ThemeMode and DefaultScanMode enums.

nodes.name: CarrierCodeStore.kt
nodes.summary: Interface for storing the user's Taiwan mobile-barcode carrier (手機條碼載具) — implementations must keep it in Keystore-backed encrypted storage, never plaintext.

nodes.name: DataStoreSettingsRepository.kt
nodes.summary: SettingsRepository backed by Preferences DataStore — maps stored keys to AppSettings with sensible defaults and exposes a reactive Flow<AppSettings>.

nodes.name: DataStoreSettingsRepository
nodes.summary: Concrete SettingsRepository using AndroidX Preferences DataStore — exposes a reactive Flow<AppSettings> and individual setter coroutines per setting.

nodes.name: EncryptedCarrierCodeStore.kt
nodes.summary: EncryptedSharedPreferences-backed CarrierCodeStore — Android Keystore master key + AES256-GCM, mirroring the database passphrase approach (ARCHITECTURE §5.2).

nodes.name: EncryptedCarrierCodeStore
nodes.summary: CarrierCodeStore implementation keeping the carrier barcode in AES256-GCM EncryptedSharedPreferences with master key from the Android Keystore.

nodes.name: SettingsRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Repository interface for reading non-sensitive app settings as a reactive Flow and writing individual fields via suspend setters.

nodes.name: SettingsModule.kt
nodes.summary: Hilt SingletonComponent module providing the Preferences DataStore, DataStoreSettingsRepository, and EncryptedCarrierCodeStore.

nodes.name: EncryptionTest.kt
nodes.summary: Android instrumentation test verifying SQLCipher encryption: data written with the correct passphrase is readable later, while an incorrect passphrase fails to decrypt the Room database.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Room's lazy decryption — the first DAO query forces SQLCipher to attempt to open the file, so the wrong-passphrase test must execute a query to assert failure.

nodes.name: EncryptionTest
nodes.summary: Instrumented test class that asserts SQLCipher passphrase enforcement on the Room invoice database by encrypting, reopening, and trying both correct and wrong passphrases.

nodes.name: InvoiceRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Defines the InvoiceRepository abstraction — the domain-level read/write contract for invoices and their line items, keeping Room/persistence types out of consumer code.
nodes.languageNotes: Default methods (getByInvoiceNumber, upsertWithItems, getItems, observeItems) give test fakes a free no-op implementation while real Room-backed impls override them.

nodes.name: InvoiceRepository
nodes.summary: Repository interface exposing suspend functions and Flow streams for invoice CRUD, dedup-by-number lookup, date-range queries, soft delete, keyword search, and line-item bundling.

nodes.name: RoomInvoiceRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Room-backed implementation of InvoiceRepository that delegates persistence to InvoiceDao/InvoiceItemDao and translates between Room entities and domain models via mappers.

nodes.name: RoomInvoiceRepository

nodes.name: TestModels.kt

nodes.name: Invoice.kt

nodes.name: Invoice
nodes.summary: Serializable data class capturing every field of a Taiwanese e-invoice including merchant/buyer tax IDs, encrypted carrier id, amounts, lottery status, source provenance, user notes/tags, and audit timestamps with soft-delete.

nodes.name: InvoiceItem.kt
nodes.summary: Domain model for a single invoice line item (品名/數量/單價/金額), serializable and parented to an Invoice by invoiceId with a sequence field for stable ordering.

nodes.name: MainDispatcherExtension.kt

nodes.name: MainDispatcherExtension
nodes.summary: BeforeEach/AfterEach JUnit 5 extension that installs a TestDispatcher (default UnconfinedTestDispatcher) as the Main dispatcher and resets it after every test.

nodes.name: McpServerControls.kt
nodes.summary: Minimal interface exposing just the running-state and token operations of McpServerManager that the settings UI needs, hiding the rest of the manager's API.

nodes.name: McpTool.kt
nodes.summary: Contract for a single MCP tool: name, description, JSON Schema for its arguments, and a suspending call that runs honouring QueryConstraints (date window + excluded categories).

nodes.name: InvoiceAnalyticsTools.kt
nodes.summary: Two analytics MCP tools: get_spending_summary aggregates totals by category/merchant/month/weekday, and get_lottery_status reports lottery counts and winners, both honouring authorization constraints.

nodes.name: GetSpendingSummaryTool
nodes.summary: McpTool that totals invoice spend grouped by category, merchant, month, or weekday over an optional date range, ordering buckets by total amount descending.

nodes.name: GetLotteryStatusTool
nodes.summary: McpTool returning per-status counts and the list of winning invoices with prizes, optionally scoped to a single 期別 (yyymm period).

nodes.name: InvoiceListingTools.kt
nodes.summary: Two listing MCP tools: list_invoices applies category/merchant/amount/date filters with pagination, and get_invoice_detail returns a single invoice with its line items, both respecting authorization constraints.

nodes.name: ListInvoicesTool
nodes.summary: McpTool that filters invoices by date range, merchant substring, category, and amount window, returning a paginated page with the total filtered count.

nodes.name: GetInvoiceDetailTool
nodes.summary: McpTool returning a single invoice (with line items) by id, or JsonNull if it's missing or filtered out by the grant's category exclusion / date window.

nodes.name: InvoiceSearchTools.kt
nodes.summary: Two discovery MCP tools: search_invoices runs keyword search across merchant/number/note, and list_merchants returns distinct merchants with visit counts and total spend.

nodes.name: SearchInvoicesTool
nodes.summary: McpTool delegating to InvoiceRepository.search for a keyword query across merchant name / invoice number / user note, then applying authorization constraints to the results.

nodes.name: ListMerchantsTool
nodes.summary: McpTool grouping invoices by merchant name to compute visit counts and lifetime spend, filterable by minimum visits and start date, sorted by visits descending.

nodes.name: ToolSupport.kt

nodes.name: ToolsTest.kt

nodes.name: ExportFormat.kt

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Binary entry point for the relay-server: loads config, opens the JSON store, constructs the relay.Server, prints the MCP HTTPS URL plus a freshly minted bearer token, and blocks on http.ListenAndServe until SIGINT/SIGTERM.
nodes.languageNotes: Idiomatic Go cmd/<svc>/main.go pattern — main is a thin wrapper around package factories.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Wires up config -> storage -> relay.Server, prints user-facing connection details (MCP URL, API token), spawns http.ListenAndServe in a goroutine, and waits on a signal channel for shutdown.

nodes.name: mintAndPrint
nodes.summary: Creates a new pairing code via srv.Pairing().Create and prints the human-facing pairing URL to stdout for the operator to scan from the phone.

nodes.name: config.go
nodes.summary: Defines the Config struct (Port, StatePath, MCPSecret, APIToken) and Load(), which reads env vars and lazily generates and persists two on-disk secrets (mcp-secret, api-token) so the same URL survives restarts.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Plain value struct holding the four runtime knobs: HTTP port, state directory path, MCP URL secret, and static API bearer token.

nodes.name: Load
nodes.summary: Reads RELAY_PORT, RELAY_STATE_DIR, ensures the state directory exists, and pins both the MCP secret and the API token to files so they persist across restarts.

nodes.name: ensureSecret
nodes.summary: Reads a secret file if it exists, otherwise mints a fresh RandomURLToken and writes it with 0600 perms — the lazy-init pattern that makes secrets stable across restarts.

nodes.name: config_test.go
nodes.summary: Verifies that Load mints a stable secret across two calls, honors RELAY_PORT, and that PairingCode/RandomURLToken produce well-formed output.

nodes.name: TestLoadGeneratesStableSecret
nodes.summary: Calls Load twice in the same temp state dir and asserts the MCPSecret is non-empty and identical — the lazy-secret persistence contract.

nodes.name: secret.go
nodes.summary: Crypto helpers: RandomURLToken returns nBytes of crypto/rand encoded as url-safe base64, and PairingCode produces an 8-char human-typeable alphanumeric code.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses crypto/rand + math/big — never math/rand — for security-sensitive token generation.

nodes.name: RandomURLToken
nodes.summary: Generates a cryptographically random URL-safe base64 token of nBytes raw entropy. Panics on rand.Read failure (treated as unrecoverable).

nodes.name: PairingCode
nodes.summary: Generates an 8-character human-readable pairing code drawn from a 32-symbol Crockford-style alphabet using crypto/rand for each position.

nodes.name: oauth.go
nodes.summary: In-memory OAuth 2.1 provider implementing dynamic client registration, authorization code + PKCE (S256), client_credentials, and bearer token validation — all backed by maps under a single mutex.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare for PKCE verification — correct constant-time discipline.

nodes.name: Provider
nodes.summary: Stateful OAuth provider holding registered clients, outstanding auth codes, and issued tokens behind a mutex; constructor injects a now() clock for testability.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: Constructs a Provider with empty client/code/token maps and an injectable clock (defaults to time.Now when nil).

nodes.name: Register
nodes.summary: Dynamic client registration: mints a fresh client_id and stores the caller-supplied redirect URI allowlist.

nodes.name: Authorize
nodes.summary: OAuth 2.1 /authorize step: validates the client, enforces S256-only PKCE method and the redirect-URI allowlist, then issues a short-lived authorization code bound to the PKCE challenge.

nodes.name: Exchange
nodes.summary: OAuth 2.1 /token authorization_code exchange: validates the code is fresh, matches client+redirect, satisfies the original PKCE challenge, and is single-use (deletes on success).

nodes.name: IssueToken
nodes.summary: client_credentials grant: validates the client is registered and mints a bearer token with TTL, returning expires_in seconds for the OAuth response.

nodes.name: Validate
nodes.summary: Bearer token introspection: returns the bound clientID if the token exists and is unexpired, deleting it lazily on expiry.

nodes.name: redirectAllowed
nodes.summary: Exact-match check against the registered redirect_uri allowlist; empty allowlist permits any URI for dev convenience.

nodes.name: oauth_test.go
nodes.summary: End-to-end OAuth provider tests covering the full PKCE auth-code flow, unknown-client rejection, S256-only enforcement, single-use codes, expiry, client_credentials, and validation edge cases.

nodes.name: TestFullAuthorizationCodeFlowWithPKCE
nodes.summary: Happy-path PKCE flow: Register -> Authorize -> Exchange -> Validate, asserting the returned token resolves back to the requesting client.

nodes.name: TestExchangeIsSingleUse
nodes.summary: Asserts that a second Exchange call with the same authorization code is rejected — single-use code enforcement, critical OAuth replay protection.

nodes.name: TestExchangeRejectsExpiredCode
nodes.summary: Advances the injected clock past the code TTL and verifies Exchange rejects the now-expired authorization code.

nodes.name: TestClientCredentialsIssuesValidToken
nodes.summary: Covers the client_credentials grant: IssueToken returns a bearer that Validate resolves; an unknown client_id is rejected.

nodes.name: TestValidateRejectsUnknownAndExpired
nodes.summary: Asserts Validate rejects both garbage tokens and tokens that have aged out, ensuring the in-memory token map cannot become an unbounded leak.

nodes.name: pairing.go
nodes.summary: Pairing service that mints short-lived human-readable codes, claims them in exchange for a long-lived device_secret + FCM token, and supports rotating the FCM token under bearer-secret auth.

nodes.name: Service
nodes.summary: Pairing domain service holding the storage handle and an injected now() clock; exposes Create/Claim/RefreshFCM to the relay HTTP layer.

nodes.name: NewService
nodes.summary: Constructs a pairing Service; defaults the clock to time.Now when nil so production callers don't have to pass one.

nodes.name: Create
nodes.summary: Mints a fresh PairingCode + expiry and persists it as a pending PairingRequest; returns the code for the operator to type into the phone.

nodes.name: Claim
nodes.summary: Phone-facing claim flow: looks up the pending pairing, enforces single-use + TTL via ConsumePairing, mints a long-lived device_secret, and persists a Device row carrying the FCM token + display name.

nodes.name: RefreshFCM
nodes.summary: Allows a paired device to rotate its FCM token by presenting its device_secret; uses constant-time secret comparison to avoid timing oracles.

nodes.name: secretEqual
nodes.summary: Length-checked constant-time string comparison wrapping crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare for device_secret authentication.

nodes.name: pairing_test.go
nodes.summary: Behavioral tests for the pairing Service: happy-path claim, unknown-code rejection, expired-code rejection, replay rejection, and FCM refresh requiring the device_secret.

nodes.name: TestClaimSucceedsAndRegistersDevice
nodes.summary: Claims a freshly created pairing and asserts a Device row is persisted with the supplied FCM token and display name.

nodes.name: TestClaimRejectsExpiredCode
nodes.summary: Advances the injected clock past pairing TTL and asserts Claim rejects the expired code with a non-nil error.

nodes.name: TestClaimRejectsReuse
nodes.summary: Verifies that a second Claim call with the same pairing code is rejected — single-use enforcement preventing device hijack on a stale code.

nodes.name: TestRefreshFCMRequiresMatchingSecret
nodes.summary: Asserts FCM token refresh fails with a wrong device_secret and succeeds with the correct one, updating the persisted Device row.

nodes.name: server.go
nodes.summary: The relay HTTP surface: composes pairing.Service, session.Manager, and oauth.Provider behind a single ServeMux exposing /pair/claim, /device/refresh, /ws, /mcp-<secret>/*, OAuth metadata + endpoints, and /healthz.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-rolled http.ServeMux + helpers (writeJSON, writeError, bearerToken) — no router framework. SSE responses are flushed manually.

nodes.name: Server
nodes.summary: Aggregate that owns every relay subsystem (config, store, pairing, sessions, websocket upgrader, OAuth provider, waker) and exposes one Handler() http.Handler wiring them all into URL routes.

nodes.name: New
nodes.summary: Constructs a Server: instantiates pairing.NewService, session.NewManager, the websocket upgrader (CheckOrigin always-true for local dev), and oauth.New with default clock.

nodes.name: Handler
nodes.summary: Builds the ServeMux: registers OAuth discovery + endpoints, the MCP path (POST + GET-405), websocket /ws, pairing /pair/claim + /device/refresh, and /healthz; wraps the whole tree in logRequests middleware.

nodes.name: logRequests
nodes.summary: Request-logging middleware that prints method, path, and duration for every incoming request — operator visibility for the single-binary deployment.

nodes.name: acceptToken
nodes.summary: Bearer-token gate for the MCP endpoint: accepts either the static APIToken (operator-known) or any OAuth-issued token still validated by the in-memory Provider.

nodes.name: handleMCP
nodes.summary: Core MCP-over-HTTPS handler: validates secret-path + bearer, parses the JSON-RPC envelope, allocates an Mcp-Session-Id on initialize, returns 202 for notifications, waker-pings the phone when its WS is down, then forwards the RPC and replies inline or as SSE.

nodes.name: inspectRPC
nodes.summary: Lightweight JSON-RPC envelope inspector — extracts id/method/isNotification without a full schema parse so the handler can branch on method type.

nodes.name: writeSSE
nodes.summary: Emits an MCP response as a single Server-Sent-Events frame (event: message + data: <json>) when the client signaled Accept: text/event-stream, then flushes the writer.

nodes.name: handleAuthServerMeta
nodes.summary: RFC 8414 OAuth Authorization Server Metadata endpoint advertising authorize/token/register URLs and the supported grant types + PKCE method.

nodes.name: handleRegister
nodes.summary: RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration endpoint — parses redirect_uris and returns a freshly minted client_id via oauth.Provider.Register.

nodes.name: handleAuthorize
nodes.summary: OAuth /authorize endpoint: pulls query params (client_id, redirect_uri, PKCE), invokes Provider.Authorize, and 302-redirects back to the client with the authorization code attached.

nodes.name: handleToken
nodes.summary: OAuth /token endpoint supporting both authorization_code (with PKCE verifier) and client_credentials grant types, returning the standard {access_token, token_type, expires_in} JSON envelope.

nodes.name: handleWS
nodes.summary: WebSocket upgrade endpoint for the phone: authenticates the bearer device_secret against the storage Device row, then hands the connection to session.Manager.Serve as the deviceID's live channel.

nodes.name: handleClaim
nodes.summary: Phone-facing /pair/claim endpoint: parses the JSON body and delegates to pairing.Service.Claim, mapping domain errors to HTTP status via claimStatus.

nodes.name: handleRefresh
nodes.summary: Phone-facing /device/refresh endpoint: bearer-auths the device_secret, parses the new FCM token, and calls pairing.Service.RefreshFCM.

nodes.name: claimStatus
nodes.summary: Maps pairing-service sentinel errors (ErrPairingNotFound, ErrPairingExpired, ErrPairingAlreadyClaimed, etc.) to HTTP status codes for consistent client behavior.

nodes.name: server_mcp_test.go
nodes.summary: End-to-end MCP-endpoint tests covering wrong-secret 404s, missing-bearer 401s, static-API-token acceptance, GET-405, notification-202, initialize sessionId+SSE behavior, forwarding to a connected phone, and FCM wake-up when the phone WS is down.

nodes.name: recordingWaker
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled fake of transport.Waker that records FCM tokens passed to Wake — Detroit-style test double instead of a mocking framework.

nodes.name: TestMCPForwardsToConnectedPhone
nodes.summary: Integration test: pairs and connects a fake phone WS, then POSTs an MCP RPC and verifies the response makes the round trip through session.Manager.Forward.

nodes.name: TestMCPStaticAPITokenAccepted
nodes.summary: Verifies that bearer-auth on the MCP endpoint accepts the operator-known static APIToken in addition to OAuth-issued tokens.

nodes.name: TestMCPInitializeSetsSessionIdAndSSE
nodes.summary: Verifies that an MCP initialize request returns an Mcp-Session-Id header and, when Accept: text/event-stream is set, emits the response as an SSE frame.

nodes.name: TestMCPWakesPhoneWhenDisconnected

nodes.name: TestMCPNotificationReturns202
nodes.summary: Asserts that a JSON-RPC notification (no id) over MCP returns 202 Accepted without waiting for a phone-side response — required by the MCP transport spec.

nodes.name: server_oauth_test.go

nodes.name: TestProtectedResourceMetadata
nodes.summary: Asserts the /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource document advertises the authorization_servers field used by MCP clients during discovery.

nodes.name: TestAuthServerMetadataAdvertisesEndpoints

nodes.name: TestClientCredentialsTokenFlow
nodes.summary: Posts grant_type=client_credentials against /token and asserts the returned bearer token gates the MCP endpoint (no token = 401, bearer = 200).

nodes.name: TestOAuthFullHTTPFlowYieldsToken
nodes.summary: Full OAuth dance over HTTP: dynamic-register a client, hit /authorize with a PKCE challenge, exchange the redirect code at /token with the verifier, then prove the access token opens the MCP endpoint.

nodes.name: server_test.go
nodes.summary: Pairing-flow HTTP integration tests for the relay: /healthz, /pair/claim happy path returning a device_secret, 404/409 error mapping, and /device/refresh requiring a valid bearer.

nodes.name: TestHealth

nodes.name: TestClaimHappyPathReturnsSecret
nodes.summary: Drives the full /pair/claim happy path through the HTTP layer and asserts the response carries a non-empty device_secret and deviceID.

nodes.name: TestClaimReuseIs409

nodes.name: TestRefreshRequiresValidSecret

nodes.name: server_ws_test.go

nodes.summary: Attempts a WS upgrade with a garbage bearer and asserts the server rejects the handshake — guarantees only the rightful phone can attach as the device's relay channel.

nodes.name: TestWSConnectAndForward

nodes.name: session.go

nodes.name: Manager

nodes.name: Conn

nodes.name: Envelope
nodes.summary: JSON envelope shuttled between Claude (MCP) and the phone (over WS): id, method, params, result, error — superset of JSON-RPC so it can carry both directions.

nodes.name: WaitConnected
nodes.summary: Blocks until the named device has a live WS or ctx fires — the synchronization point that lets handleMCP wake the phone via FCM and then wait for it to come online.

nodes.name: Serve
nodes.summary: Per-device read loop: registers the new Conn, fans out connect-waiters, then reads incoming JSON envelopes and dispatches each to its waiting pending-RPC channel until the WS closes.

nodes.name: Forward
nodes.summary: Sends an MCP envelope to the named device's WS and waits up to a timeout for the matching response envelope; returns ErrNotConnected if no Conn is registered.

nodes.name: deliver
nodes.summary: Looks up the pending-RPC channel for an incoming envelope's id, non-blockingly sends the response, and removes the entry — the matcher half of the request/response pairing.

nodes.name: TestForwardTimesOut

nodes.name: RelayAuditLog

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the top-level README to learn what Invoice Wallet is: a local-first Taiwan e-invoice wallet (Android) paired with a tiny Go relay so your own AI assistants can query receipts that never leave your phone. The README enumerates the three AI access paths (Claude Mobile via Cloudflare-tunnelled relay, Claude Desktop via ADB/LAN MCP, other Android AI via Content Provider) that the rest of the tour traces through real code. The Traditional Chinese counterpart README.zh.md mirrors the same content for ZH readers.

tour.title: Canonical Architecture Spec
tour.description: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md is the v2 design document the codebase is built against — it pins down the five Room entities (Invoice / InvoiceItem / LotteryNumber / AuthGrant / QueryAuditLog) you will see in Step 6, the minimal relay SQLite schema you will see in Step 13, the secret-URL pairing protocol from Step 10, and the phased 0–6 roadmap. Read this once and the module names in the rest of the tour will line up with named boxes in the spec.

tour.title: Android Entry Point
tour.description: MainActivity is the single-Activity Hilt entry point. It reads settings from AppViewModel and decides between OnboardingScreen (first run) and the real shell, applying the user-selected ThemeMode through InvoiceWalletTheme. InvoiceWalletApplication is the Hilt @HiltAndroidApp container that bootstraps the DI graph for every module the tour will visit. AndroidManifest.xml registers the activity, declares CAMERA + INTERNET permissions, and points to the adaptive launcher icon.
tour.languageLesson: Kotlin + Hilt: @HiltAndroidApp on Application generates the DI container at compile time; @AndroidEntryPoint on the Activity injects fields from that graph. A single Activity hosting Compose NavHost is the modern Android convention — Fragments are no longer required.

tour.title: Compose Navigation Shell
tour.description: InvoiceWalletApp is the root Composable: a Scaffold that hosts WalletNavBar as the bottom bar plus a NavHost wiring the three top-level tabs (發票 / 對獎 / 設定) and the scan, detail, and pairing sub-routes. Building on the entry point from Step 3, this is where the feature-module Composables you'll meet later (invoice-list, lottery, settings, scan, invoice-detail, pairing) are actually plugged into routes. The in-file ScanRoute owns camera-permission flow, image-picking, and snackbar feedback for the camera screen.
tour.languageLesson: Jetpack Compose: NavHost + composable(route = ...) replaces the old XML navigation graph. Scaffold provides slots (topBar, bottomBar, content) instead of inheritance — composition over configuration is the Compose-wide pattern.

tour.title: Scanning Receipts (the Core Loop)
tour.description: The scan feature is what users do first and most often — point the camera at a printed receipt and capture its data. EInvoiceQrParser handles the gnarly real-world inputs: ROC + Gregorian dates, CP950 encoding, gas-station POSes that omit 自定區, and decimal qty/price. ScanViewModel orchestrates camera state, parser output, OCR fallback, merchant lookup, and the eventual save into the InvoiceRepository from Step 6. CameraQrScanner drives CameraX with a per-QR detection polygon, and the einvoice-qr-fixtures.json corpus is the source of truth the parser tests are driven from.

tour.title: The Domain Model
tour.description: The pure-JVM :core:model module defines the vocabulary every other module speaks. Invoice (fan-in 34, by far the most-depended-on file in the codebase) and InvoiceItem are kotlinx-serialization data classes with no Android dependencies, which is why they can flow from the scan parser to the database to the MCP tool surface to the relay-server's JSON-RPC tunnel unchanged. LotteryNumber is what the lottery matcher in Step 8 compares against.
tour.languageLesson: kotlinx.serialization with @Serializable + value classes: domain types double as wire types without a separate DTO layer. Keeping :core:model as a pure-JVM module (no android.* imports) means it compiles fast and tests run off-device.

tour.title: Encrypted Persistence
tour.description: The :core:database module owns durability. InvoiceWalletDatabase is the Room database, DatabaseModule is the Hilt graph that wires DAOs and repositories, and Mappers.kt translates between persistence-shape entities (enums-as-strings) and the typed domain models from Step 6. The crucial security primitive is DatabasePassphraseProvider, which derives the SQLCipher passphrase from a Keystore-wrapped key — that is what 'your receipts stay on your phone' actually means at the bytes level. The exported schema v1 JSON is the contract MigrationTestHelper compares against to detect drift.
tour.languageLesson: Room + SQLCipher: Room generates DAO implementations at compile time from @Dao interfaces. Wrapping it with SQLCipher means every SQL byte on disk is AES-encrypted; the passphrase lives only in memory after Keystore unwraps it. Schema JSON exports give you a diffable artifact for every migration.

tour.title: Lottery Matching
tour.description: Taiwan runs a bimonthly public lottery against e-invoice numbers; the :feature:lottery module is how the app turns that into a tap-to-check-winnings screen. LotteryApiClient fetches the Ministry of Finance winning numbers via Ktor; LotteryMatcher applies the Taiwan-specific rules (special / 特別 / 頭獎 / 二獎 / …) against the invoices already in your encrypted DB from Step 7; LotteryViewModel exposes the matched results to LotteryScreen.

tour.title: The Vocabulary Design System
tour.description: The :core:design-system module is the editorial 'Vocabulary by Acumotion' DSL referenced in the README — a small Compose component library every feature consumes so the app reads as one coherent product instead of a collection of screens. WalletTheme (fan-in 16) holds the colors / typography / shapes / spacing tokens; PillButton / CompactPill / WalletNavBar are the three components that show up everywhere. CategoryGuesser is the heuristic that maps a merchant name into one of the eight watercolour categories surfaced as a CategoryBadge on each invoice card.

tour.title: AI Path A — Pairing With the Relay
tour.description: Path A from the README: Claude Mobile/Web → Cloudflare Tunnel → Go relay → phone WebSocket. This step is the phone side of how that link gets established. PairingClient redeems the one-shot QR code from the relay (the wire format lives in spec/pairing-protocol.md, opened in Step 14); RelayUrl validates the pasted https://... URL; PairingViewModel drives the UI. Once paired, RelayManager from the :data-source:relay-client module keeps the WebSocket connection alive and hands incoming JSON-RPC frames to RelayMessageHandler, which forwards them into the in-app MCP server you'll meet in Step 11.

tour.title: AI Path B — In-App MCP Server
tour.description: Path B from the README: Claude Desktop → ADB reverse or LAN → in-app Ktor MCP server. McpServerManager runs a Ktor CIO server inside the app; McpServerRouting exposes the /mcp endpoint; McpDispatcher decodes JSON-RPC requests and dispatches to the typed tools listed in spec/mcp-tools.md (list_invoices, get_invoice_detail, search_invoices, get_spending_summary, get_lottery_status, list_merchants). InvoiceListingTools is one of those tool implementations and shows the read-only pattern they all follow — pull from the InvoiceRepository, project into the <invoice> XML schema, return.
tour.languageLesson: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a JSON-RPC 2.0 dialect: clients send tools/list and tools/call; servers reply with structured content. Ktor CIO embedded inside an Android app gives you an HTTP server with no JVM-only dependencies — the same code can also be hosted by the Go relay's WebSocket tunnel.

tour.title: Authorization & Audit
tour.description: Because both AI paths reach the same user data, every MCP call passes through AuthorizationEngine before it can read anything. It consults AuthGrant records (Step 6's domain type, persisted by AuthGrantRepository) to decide whether a given client + tool combination is allowed, and writes a QueryAuditLog row for every approved call so the user can review later who asked what. This is the security seam that lets the README claim 'under a key only you hold' even while remote AI agents are talking to the wallet.

tour.title: The Go Relay Server
tour.description: The relay-server is the other half of Path A — a self-hosted Go binary you run on a Raspberry Pi or laptop so Claude Mobile can reach your phone through the public internet without anyone in the middle holding your data. cmd/relay/main.go boots the process; internal/relay/server.go (fan-out 16, the most wired-up file in the repo) is the HTTP surface exposing the five routes documented in relay-server/README.md (/health, /pair/claim, /device/refresh, /ws, /mcp-<secret>/); internal/pairing/pairing.go implements the server side of the same protocol the Android PairingClient from Step 10 talks to; internal/storage/storage.go persists the minimal JSON store. go.mod pins the project's deliberately tiny dependency footprint — pure Go plus gorilla/websocket.
tour.languageLesson: Go HTTP services: net/http handlers are functions of (ResponseWriter, *Request). gorilla/websocket upgrades a regular HTTP request into a long-lived bidirectional connection — perfect for the phone's WSS tunnel because it traverses Cloudflare and home-router NAT without any extra plumbing.

tour.title: Build Infrastructure, CI, and Wire Specs
tour.description: Closing the loop: how the whole monorepo gets built, tested, and shipped. libs.versions.toml is the single source of truth for every Android dependency version (AGP 8.7.3, Kotlin 2.0.21, Compose BOM, Hilt, Ktor, ML Kit, zxing-cpp, CameraX) referenced by every module's build.gradle.kts via the convention plugins. The android.yml GitHub Actions workflow runs ktlint + unit tests + assembleDebug on every PR. Then the two spec files — mcp-tools.md and pairing-protocol.md — are the wire contracts that lock down what Step 10's pairing flow and Step 11's MCP tools must do, independent of any implementation language; they're the documents the Android and Go halves of the repo both agree to.
tour.languageLesson: Gradle Version Catalogs (libs.versions.toml): one TOML file declares every dependency coordinate + version once; modules reference them as libs.androidx.compose.bom etc. This eliminates the classic 'three modules at three different Kotlin versions' drift problem and gives Renovate-style bots a single file to update.
